tasks.short: Create dressing lists, show notes and costume checks

steps.what: Read the actual current script, cast list and wardrobe change instructions in {DOCS}, checking the production revision.
inputs: Actual current script, cast list and wardrobe instructions
outputs: Actual source package for costume worksheets

steps.what: Draft the dressing-list scene sequence, cast entries and costume-change cues in the worksheet {SPREADSHEET} from the actual script and instructions.
outputs: Draft dressing-list entries with source cues

loop.purpose: Draft dressing-list entries from the actual script
loop.input: Current permitted script, cast list and wardrobe instructions selected in s1
loop.output: Draft scene/cast/change rows with source references and ambiguity flags
loop.check: Attendant checks actual cues, practical change sequence and wardrobe meaning in s6, beyond the exact-name check in s5
loop.stop: One draft and one correction, then manual entry; ambiguous cues are never inferred
loop.why_not_simpler: Native worksheet templates are used first, but script directions and wardrobe notes can describe a change in free text rather than structured rows.

steps.what: Enter the actual garment identifiers, dressing positions, observed show notes and costume-check facts in {SPREADSHEET}, resolving them from actual wardrobe work rather than the script alone.
inputs: Actual wardrobe, rehearsal observations and garment identities
outputs: Actual completed worksheet entries and show notes

steps.what: Sort and format the actual entries into dressing lists, show-note sheets and costume-check worksheets using native {SPREADSHEET} views and print layouts.
outputs: Draft formatted costume worksheets

steps.what: Compare the worksheet cast and garment identifiers against the actual approved cast list and wardrobe identifiers using exact native lookup rules {SPREADSHEET}.
inputs: Actual approved identifiers from s1 and s3
outputs: Literal unmatched-name and garment-id flags

steps.what: Check and correct the complete worksheets against the actual script, costume requirements and rehearsal changes, verifying that the dressing sequence and show notes mean the right thing.
inputs: Complete worksheets and exact-match flags from s4-s5
outputs: Corrected usable costume worksheets

steps.what: Save the actual worksheets in the same production {SPREADSHEET} workspace.
outputs: Saved current costume worksheets

tasks.design: Use native {SPREADSHEET} tables, exact lookups and print views for the actual costume worksheets. A bounded script-reading loop may draft dressing-list rows, but the attendant supplies actual wardrobe facts and verifies the complete practical sequence and show-note meaning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Script directions and actual wardrobe observations must be turned into repeatable worksheet layouts.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views handle sorting and format, while a bounded draft can expose script cues with source references.
tasks.still_hard: A scene cue does not establish how a particular performer can safely complete a quick change.
tasks.human_edge: Know the costume, performer and backstage constraints behind the worksheet.

ambition.what: Provide a source-linked cover-dresser worksheet for an understudy performance.

tasks.altitude: Less reformatting; wardrobe sequence decisions and actual show observations remain human.

reach.learn: Connect costume and makeup cues without assuming the same backstage timing.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 for script rights and production records

evidence.claim: Native worksheets can sort and format explicit scene/cast/garment rows; a script-derived draft still needs practical wardrobe checking.

assumptions: Boundary is the explicit worksheet task, including current-source reading, actual wardrobe facts and final practical checking. Rehearsal, fitting and physical dressing work are unchanged and earn no saving here.

Production owners supply the actual script revision, scene/cue labels and cast ids. s3 counts the attendant's actual capture of garment id, position, show observation and check result. Missing or ambiguous cues return to manual reading; there is no free structured wardrobe feed.

Conditional E1 shares, not measured baselines. Native tables and print views are tested first. s4 removes only repeated sorting/layout, s5 only literal identifier comparison, s2 only part of narrative-to-row drafting; no single cut is applied to all configured work. Existing automatic views earn no saving. Internal saving is fully retained and ungated.
unknowns: Are script cues and cast identifiers stable?
How much sorting/layout is still manual?
research_questions: Do complete worksheets preserve actual quick-change meaning after rehearsal revisions?

already_counted.description: Actual source reading, draft review, wardrobe-fact capture and practical worksheet checking

incremental.description: Maintain print views and audit cue/name mappings after script revisions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10 draft composition plus 20 sorting/layout plus 5 literal matching = 35, minus 2 upkeep gives 33. Conservative case: changing script labels and unstable garment identities make rows incompatible with the views, requiring manual drafting and layout; retain the current worksheet method. Actual wardrobe capture and complete practical checking remain in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist cast dressing and assign dressers

steps.what: Choose actual dresser-to-cast assignments for the performance using the current change sequence, availability and practical backstage needs.
inputs: Actual dressing list and available dressers
outputs: Actual dresser assignments

steps.what: Mark actual dresser assignments on the performance dressing sheet.
outputs: Actual assignment marks on the dressing sheet

steps.what: Brief the actual dressers and cast on their assigned changes and clarify last-minute practical constraints.
outputs: Assignments understood by cast and dressers

steps.what: Provide actual dressing assistance to cast members, handling garments and fastenings and responding to costume-change difficulties during the performance.
inputs: Actual performer, costumes and performance cues
outputs: Actual dressing assistance and completed costume changes

tasks.design: Retain actual assignment choices, the assignment marks on the existing dressing sheet, the live briefing and physical dressing assistance. A native digital assignment view would change the surface, but it does not remove the new assignment decision or mark in this direct backstage workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rapid costume changes depend on real people, space and garments.
tasks.enabler_now: No new tool is needed for the actual assignment-and-assistance sequence.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected garment failures and last-minute cast changes need immediate practical coordination.
tasks.human_edge: Help the performer and coordinate dressers sensitively under time pressure.
tasks.altitude: No change in assignment rights or physical assistance.

reach.learn: Recognise shared quick-change constraints while preserving separate craft duties.

evidence.claim: A digital assignment surface does not itself remove actual assignment choices, live coordination or physical dressing assistance.

assumptions: Boundary includes both assignment and dressing assistance. The actual assignment write is explicitly separate from the conversation; no extra post-performance record, save or report is invented.

The performance dressing list already exists from the worksheet workflow; actual availability and practical needs are established in s1. s2 records only the new assignment. There is no assumed automatic staff-availability feed or worker-ranking model.

Conditional E1 shares. Native assignment views are considered but no duplicate entry or reducible list-generation action is evidenced here. Actual assignment marks and physical work retain their time. With no adopted tool or process change, incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Is there a genuine duplicate assignment transfer in the actual production?
research_questions: Observe the current assignment sheet and briefing before proposing any new assignment software.

already_counted.description: Actual assignment decision, separate assignment marks, live briefing and dressing help

incremental.description: No new tool or process to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: After splitting the actual assignment record, the proposed native view still removes no evidenced action. The decision, assignment marks, briefing and physical help remain; no trailing report or storage baseline is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design, construct or send costumes for tailoring

steps.what: Design the actual costume or alteration approach from the character, fabric, performer and production requirements.
inputs: Actual production concept, performer and fabric requirements
outputs: Actual costume design and work scope

steps.what: Construct the actual costume elements within the department's capability, cutting, sewing and handling materials for the intended design.
outputs: Actual constructed costume elements

steps.what: Check the actual costume and decide which construction, major repair or alteration work needs the tailor, confirming the required measurements and finish.
outputs: Actual tailor work requirements and garment identity

steps.what: Write the actual tailor job card in {DOCS}, including garment identity, required work, measurements and due performance, with native repeated production fields.
outputs: Complete tailor job card and garment dispatch details

steps.what: Check the complete job card against the actual garment, design intent, measurements and selected tailor before dispatch, correcting discrepancies.
inputs: Actual garment and work requirements from s3
outputs: Checked final job card v1 and exact garment/destination match

steps.what: Save the actual final tailor job card in the same {DOCS} production workspace.
inputs: Final job card v1 from s5
outputs: Saved final job card v1

steps.what: Send the exact matched costume and final job card to the specified tailor for the required construction, major repair or alteration.
inputs: Actual garment and checked destination from s5
Unchanged final job card v1 from s6
outputs: Tailor receives the actual garment and work instructions

tasks.design: Use native repeated production fields in the actual tailor job card {DOCS}. Costume design, construction, fitting decisions, actual work instructions and the garment handoff remain human; the separate dispatch uses the completed checked job card, while internal saving has no gate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Production identifiers can be copied repeatedly onto tailor cards.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields can reuse those identifiers without generating alteration requirements.
tasks.still_hard: Fabric behaviour, movement and the character's appearance determine a suitable alteration.
tasks.human_edge: Translate the physical costume and design intent into accurate practical instructions.

ambition.what: Reduce small repeated headers without changing craft work.

tasks.altitude: No change in design or tailoring decisions.

reach.learn: Preserve design continuity across costume and makeup changes.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2 for production identifiers and performer measurements

evidence.claim: Native job-card fields can reuse production identifiers; actual costume work and alteration instructions remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is the attendant's actual design/construction work and the explicit tailor-send branch, including its actual job card. Supplier tailoring labour stays unchanged and outside the attendant's savings. No purchasing or courier administration baseline is added.

s3 produces actual garment id, required alteration, measurements and finish; s4 records them. Existing production records supply production id and performance/date. Missing fields require manual work. Only repeated headers change; no fit measurement or design intent is inferred.

Conditional E1 shares for a mixed in-house/tailor work cycle, not measured baseline. Native fields are tested first. The dispatch gate is the actual garment/instruction/destination check after the complete card exists, not an approval of an ordinary author save. Any changed card or garment match requires fresh checking before s7.
unknowns: Does the department use actual tailor job cards with repeated headers?
research_questions: Does the job card preserve exact measurements, garment identity and intended finish at handoff?

already_counted.description: Actual design, construction, work definition, job-card writing, garment matching and dispatch

approvals.approved_version: Exact final job card v1, actual garment and tailor destination checked at the end of s5; unchanged at s6; any mismatch voids dispatch clearance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15*0.10 = 1.5 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 1. Conservative case: one-off cards have no repeated production headers or existing cards already populate them, so retain the current job-card method. Craft work, new measurements, final garment check and physical dispatch stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine fit and write alteration notes

steps.what: Examine actual costume fit on the cast member, checking comfort, appearance, movement and performance needs.
inputs: Actual cast member wearing the costume
outputs: Actual observed fit issues

steps.what: Decide the actual alterations, confirming measurements, fabric allowances and intended visual effect with the performer where needed.
inputs: Actual garment construction and performer feedback
outputs: Actual alteration decisions and measurements

steps.what: Sketch or write the actual alteration notes, identifying the garment, location, measurement and intended change on the fitting sheet.
inputs: Actual alteration decisions and measurements from s2
outputs: Actual alteration sketch or written fitting notes

steps.what: Keep the actual fitting sheet with the identified costume's working records.
outputs: Available fitting instructions for the actual garment

tasks.design: Retain the physical fitting and the explicitly separate alteration sketch or note. A native form or standard sketch sheet can organise the fields, but it does not supply the actual new measurements, garment-specific change or drawing; do not add a second digital record solely to create a saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: The correct alteration depends on this garment on this performer.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is needed for the actual fitting-sheet workflow.
tasks.still_hard: A fit that looks right standing still may restrict performance movement.
tasks.human_edge: Judge material behaviour, appearance and comfort together.
tasks.altitude: No change in fitting or alteration responsibility.

reach.learn: Discuss movement and comfort without losing the character's visual intent.

evidence.claim: A fitting-sheet template does not replace physical fit assessment or the actual new alteration measurements and sketch.

assumptions: Boundary includes the explicit examination and alteration-note work. The actual sketch/write step is separate from the physical fitting; keeping that working sheet is ordinary storage, not a new trailing report.

The attendant produces actual observations in s1 and measurements/decisions in s2; s3 captures garment id, alteration location, amount and intent. No camera fit inference, structured measurement feed or free extraction is assumed.

Conditional E1 shares. Native form/standard sketch-sheet options are considered, but no repeated transcription or removable formatting step is evidenced in this direct sheet workflow. New garment-specific information remains fully retained.
No tool or process change is adopted, so incremental upkeep is zero. Ordinary fitting-sheet storage has no approval stage or saving.
unknowns: Is the actual fitting sheet copied elsewhere by hand?
research_questions: Observe the existing sketch/note process before proposing a template reduction; distinguish actual drawing and new measurements from repeated fields.

already_counted.description: Actual fitting, alteration decisions, separate sketch/notes and working-sheet storage

time_saved_range_pct.basis: After separating the explicit alteration note, no evidenced action is removed by a standard sheet: physical fitting, measurements, garment-specific sketch/write and keeping the working sheet remain. No extra duplicate record or approval process is introduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less repeated worksheet composition and formatting; physical costume care, fitting and performer help remain human.
reach: Coordinate actual change cues with theatrical makeup colleagues
role.ambitious_version: Useful costume worksheets that reflect real garments and performers rather than an inferred script alone.
